Grove endpoint checks: the compiled 64-bit domain

The exact mutation changes the first pair of endpoint checks in NewGrove
from !indexable(lo.X) || !indexable(hi.X) to their conjunction. This is
redundant on the tested 64-bit target. It is NOT a portable logical
equivalence of two arbitrary ranges.

Construction establishes a positive finite cell width c at least as large
as every canopy radius r. The centre coordinate a is binary64. Its vector
length must be finite, so |a| is at most sqrt(MaxFloat64), below 2^513.
The endpoint operations a-r and a+r cannot overflow: if r is in the largest
binary64 binade, a is far below half its ULP and both sums round to +/-r;
otherwise r+|a| stays below the overflow threshold. Neither division by the
positive finite c can produce NaN.

The only way an endpoint can fail indexable on a 64-bit host is for its
floored normalized coordinate to reach the index boundary, about +/-2^63,
or overflow to infinity. Conservatively, an offending endpoint has exact
magnitude at least 2^62*c, allowing ample room for rounding. Since r<=c,
the centre then has |a|>2^61*c, hence r<2^-61*|a|.

The centre is normal: even the smallest positive c=2^-1074 gives
|a|>2^-1013, above the minimum normal 2^-1022. For a normal binary64 centre,
half the smaller adjacent spacing is at least 2^-55*|a|, including a binade
boundary. Thus r is less than 1/64 of that half-spacing. Both a-r and a+r
round to the SAME stored centre a. Their subsequent division and floor
are identical, so both endpoints have the same indexability.

If neither endpoint is outside, both checks are false anyway. Therefore
their disjunction and conjunction make the same constructor decision in
this isolated mutation on the compiled 64-bit public canopy domain.

The distinction matters on 32-bit targets. With c=r=1 and a=MinInt32,
lo=MinInt32-1 is outside while hi=MinInt32+1 fits. The retained 32-bit test
checks this real canopy and a nearby valid control. It also avoids a
runaway mutant: even if conversion is wrong, an accepted range ending at
MinInt+1 can walk at most two X buckets. Game still runs mutations before
classifying surviving equivalents, so this test kills the mutation on
those targets rather than letting the 64-bit exception conceal it.

Review this argument if the cell/radius relation, coordinate type, finite
centre check, endpoint arithmetic, index bounds or target word size changes.
The 32-bit test is not claimed as runtime-tested on this Darwin/ARM64 host;
cross-compilation is a separate check, and its result must be recorded.
Source hashes and actual target metadata belong with the installed proof.
